bull.b: The latest balance sheet reduces immediate financial leverage risk, giving CalciMedica greater flexibility while it advances clinical programs. Positive equity also provides a stronger base than periods when equity was negative, although continued losses could erode this position.

Additional funding gives the company time to execute clinical and IND-enabling work without an immediate financing deadline. A longer runway can support value creation from Auxora and CM5480 milestones, despite the financing’s dilution implications.

The absence of FDA objections or a clinical hold supports continued development of Auxora and reduces near-term regulatory uncertainty. Progress across acute kidney injury, pulmonary hypertension and other inflammatory indications preserves multiple potential paths for the CRAC platform.

bear.b: Without commercialized products or recurring revenue, CalciMedica cannot currently fund operations from customers. Its future depends on clinical success, regulatory approvals and external financing, making the business model inherently dependent on uncertain development outcomes.

Material ongoing losses show that the company remains far from self-sustaining operations. Even though losses improved versus 2025, profitability depends on successful clinical development and eventual commercialization, while prolonged losses can reduce financial flexibility.

bear.t: High cash burn and dilution risk
bear.b: Sustained negative cash flow requires repeated access to capital before revenue emerges. Recent equity, warrant and equity-plan actions expand financing flexibility but can increase future share issuance, ownership dilution and pressure on existing investors.
